newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end down on low turnover.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end down on low turnover.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Tuesday in dull trading which saw investors taking to the sidelines as they waited to get in at lower levels, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.8 points lower at 612.6, in line with the downward trend the market has been experiencing during the past week.
Turnover, in the absence of foreign and retail activity, was a dismal 8.2 million rupees, down from Monday's 47.8 million rupees. Losses dominated, outnumbering gains 38 to seven.
"It was a dried up situation. People were just watching, rather than doing anything," said Rohan Fernando, manager operations at C.T. Smith Stockbrokers.
Retail investors who took the all share index up from around 608 points in late October, were waiting enter at lower levels, a broker for Bartleet Mallory said.
"Retailers are out of the market. They are taking a back seat rather than moving in at this level," the broker said.
Othger brokers said the market was correcting after having risen from 550 to 630 points in about two months.
